lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.criterion: Full-viewport retrieval hierarchy and restrained shell material
findings.observation: At English AX5, result count and Synthetic preview occupy two fixed lines and the full composer remains prominent during scrolling. At regular size the pale composer outline and broad shadow also carry more elevation than the mostly flat retrieval list. Large text and scrolling are supported, and neither is treated as a failure.
findings.evidence: iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 frozen round-2: 07-sessions-ax5.png, 08-people-ax5.png, 09-sessions-ax5-scrolled.png and 10-people-ax5-scrolled.png show the unchanged utility shelf across first/subsequent viewports; 01-sessions-light.png, 03-people-light.png and 04-people-filter.png show the prominent composer material.
findings.user_impact: The recruiter has less usable viewport for reading identity, context and recency together, and the supporting input surface retains considerable visual priority while retrieving existing content.
findings.recommendation: Allow count and Synthetic preview to share a line when their actual rendered widths fit at AX5, keep all disclosure and commands readable, and soften the composer's surrounding shadow.
findings.verification: Recapture the same first/subsequent AX5 viewports and regular light states. Preserve requested text sizes, search/filter/page access, full synthetic disclosure and 44-point command targets while reducing unnecessary utility height/elevation.

findings.criterion: Adaptive row grouping, alignment and status icon restraint
findings.observation: AX5 People uses a separate initials/menu row before the name. Its separator keeps the regular avatar-column inset even though the text uses the full-width leading edge. In AX5 Sessions, the Review needed symbol grows into a large dotted ring beside the already explicit two-line label.
findings.evidence: Frozen round-2 08-people-ax5.png shows the LH/menu accessory-only row before Leila; 10-people-ax5-scrolled.png shows the inset rule beneath full-width recency and the next accessory row; compare 03-people-light.png. 09-sessions-ax5-scrolled.png shows the large dotted ring; compare its compact treatment in 01-sessions-light.png. These are actual scroll positions, not clipped exports.
findings.user_impact: Ancillary elements interrupt identity grouping and retain geometry from a different layout. The large status symbol adds visual urgency without improving the text's meaning.
findings.recommendation: Recompose AX5 accessories around the text: group the avatar/menu with the name, align rules to the active text column, and keep the review symbol subordinate to the full-size readable label.
findings.verification: Capture matching AX5 People and Sessions states after any change. Confirm the first person's menu remains hittable and at least 44 by 44 points, identity and complete context remain reachable, the rule follows the text column, and review attention still has a readable non-color label.

findings.observation: Both Chinese dark People rows retain the English Candidate label alongside localized navigation, counts and recency. English names, employers and search titles are accepted as workspace content.
findings.evidence: Frozen round-2 06-people-dark-zh.png, Leila and Nia rows: Candidate precedes localized 2周前; shell labels include 人物 and 搜索人物.
findings.user_impact: A visible person-kind label breaks the otherwise consistent Chinese retrieval shell and introduces avoidable language switching.
findings.recommendation: Confirm that Candidate is app-owned person-kind copy, then localize that label while preserving stored names, employers and search titles.
findings.verification: Recapture Chinese People with the same synthetic data; app-owned labels should follow the locale and the identity/context strings should remain unchanged.

strengths: All ten full-viewport screenshots were inspected. Regular Sessions makes topic primary and keeps candidate/search context and recency readable; 01 versus 02 and mixed-state 05 visibly separate unread treatment from review attention.
People names, current role/employer and search context form a clear retrieval hierarchy in 03/04/06. One-result filtering stays honestly sparse, with an explicit scope chip and remove command in 04.
Sessions and People use the same page selection, search/filter controls, menu positions and warm light/dark materials. Utility copy is quiet at regular size.
AX5 wraps content instead of truncating essential strings. 09 and 10 provide subsequent scroll evidence; partial text at a live viewport boundary is not treated as permanently hidden content.

The frozen input reports focused policy/native checks covering retrieval handlers, read-state composition, restoration and the first AX5 People menu target. Reported CUA readback distinguishes Read session, Unread and Review needed. This supports the bounded specialist score without claiming direct runtime validation.
missing_evidence: Evidence level 4 for personally inspected artifacts: screenshots only, supplemented by the frozen input's behavioral summary. Raw xcresult bundles, application code and accessibility trees were not inspected and no direct interaction was performed.

Search/filter/reset, restoration and content access are reported tested. The ten PNGs do not independently demonstrate all transitions, empty results, open filter/menu states, keyboard behavior or all command hit areas; the first People AX5 menu is the explicit reported 44-point target check.

VoiceOver order/focus/actions, rendered accessibility conformance, real-device ergonomics, latency and interruption/recovery remain unverified by this reviewer. Token contrast formulas and CUA readback do not establish those properties.

The input states identity, provenance, persistence and external-write authorization semantics were not intentionally changed; this bounded screenshot review does not independently prove those gates. No failed gate or veto is observed.

The frozen image set has no Chinese dark AX5 capture or long-dataset visual sequence, although the input reports relevant native checks. No first-use recruiter comprehension or field-usefulness evidence is supplied.
open_questions: Is the visible Candidate value in the Chinese People surface app-owned localized person-kind copy or a stored workspace value?
